newsitem.title: USA: No frost threat to Brazil coffee--U.S. forecasters.
newsitem.headline: No frost threat to Brazil coffee--U.S. forecasters.

text.p: A cold front expected to push into southern Brazil later this week is not expected to cause any damage to the country's coffee belt, U.S. weather forecasters said Wednesday.

While a high pressure system in central Argentina is forecast to bring colder weather to Brazil by Thursday into the weekend, temperatures are not expected to drop low enough to cause frost in coffee-growing areas.

"This pattern has the potential to bring much colder air into the southern portions of the coffee belt later this week," WSC said. "However, it is not expected to be cold enough to cause any damage as it is too early in the season for a damaging freeze to occur."
The earliest damaging frost on record was May 31. The Brazilian coffee regions face the greatest cold weather risks in the months of June and July.

"The time of year is simply unfavorable for there to be a damage event," said Smith Barney meteorolgist Jon Davis in his daily forecast. "This is because at this point in the fall, the sun angle is still high enough in the sky and the days are long enough to greatly reduce the chances of a cold airmass being strong enough to drop temps to the levels to cause damage this far north."
Davis said temperatures on Sunday and Monday -- the day's expected to be the coldest -- will fall into the 40s F.
"These readings are unusually cold for this time of year," he said. "But not down to levels which would cause damage to the developing beans or more importantly, the trees themselves."
Temperatures are expected to return to more normal levels next week, Davis added.
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk, 212 859 1640
